svg.text: MapForge Pro — Logistics Intelligence Suite · Architecture

JavaFX desktop monolith (package com.storemapper, artifact mapforge-pro 1.5) — one app, dual GUI + CLI entry · 8 planning tools · clustering & coverage algorithms · Google APIs + GeoTools / JTS / POI. Not microservices — a layered desktop app.
dashed green = call out to an external service / library
UML class box: name / fields / methods · «@stereotype» or «interface» shown in the header
Layer colour coding (consistent across all views)

2 · Layered class view — Shell → UI → Tools → Algorithms / Utils → Model
Each tool runs its heavy work on a background JavaFX Task; the same tools also power the CLI. Utilities wrap I/O, Google APIs and spatial libraries.
sidebar nav hosts every tool view
runs the tool on a JavaFX background Task
gathers inputs → calls its Tool on a Task

within an SLA radius; builds map
SlaRadiusCalibrator (grows radius to hit target coverage)
strategy pattern — the tool picks one impl at runtime
by the algorithm the user selected
util — I/O, spatial, maps, API access
Console: ConsoleHelper (prompts & formatting for the CLI)
model — immutable data holders passed between layers (~28 records / POJOs)
Store · Pincode · Candidate · CandidateSite · ClusterResult · ClusterOutput · DistanceResult · DemandCell · SelectedStore
PlannerParams · PlannerResult · PlannerWorkspace · PlannerSource · SlaPlannerInput · SlaPlannerSettings · PincodeServiceability
StoreScorecard · StoreCoverage · TileResult · RoadFact · NibRecord · NibAssignment · StemMetric · ValidatedResult · CustomerRecord …
no logic — just typed fields the UI, tools, algorithms and utils read and write
in: CSV · Excel · GeoJSON · Shapefile · GeoPackage
out: Excel · CSV · Leaflet HTML maps · GeoJSON
All data lives on the local machine; the only network
calls are the two Google APIs (with cost estimation).
runs the tool on a background Task
3 · Runtime — one desktop process: User → GUI/CLI → Tool on a Task → algorithms/utils → Google APIs + files
• GUI → the ProgressPane bar updates live
• CLI → percentage lines print to the console
ResultPane shows the summary when done.

Read it as: ① user opens the app (GUI or CLI) → ② picks a tool & inputs → ③ tool runs the chosen algorithm + utils on a Task → ④ utils call Google APIs (results cached) and read/write local spatial files
→ ⑤ outputs are written as Excel/CSV plus a Leaflet HTML map. Everything is one JVM process on the analyst's machine — there is no server, no database, no network except the two Google APIs.

Threading note: the GUI never blocks — each tool's work is wrapped in a javafx.concurrent.Task, and progress flows back through the ProgressCallback seam so the same tool code serves both GUI and CLI.
4 · Trace — running the "Demand Clustering" tool end to end

g.text: Open Demand Clustering in the sidebar (WarehouseClusteringView).
Pick the input CSV, set K, choose an algorithm and a distance method.
On Run, the view starts a JavaFX Task and calls WarehouseClusteringTool.run(…).
CsvHelper loads the rows; the tool builds demand-weighted points (DemandCell).
The chosen ClusterAlgorithm.cluster(points, K) returns a ClusterResult (centroids + assignments).
Distances: GeoUtil haversine, or GoogleApiClient road distances cached in RoadDistanceCache.
MapGenerator writes a Leaflet HTML map; ExcelHelper writes the assignment workbook.
ProgressCallback drives the ProgressPane; ResultPane shows the summary and the map opens.

svg.text: Geodesic mode needs no API key and no network
— fully offline. Google mode adds road-accurate
distances and estimates the API cost first.
# the same run from the CLI
→ same Tool, same algorithms, no GUI
The other seven tools follow the same shape:
a view gathers inputs → a Tool runs on a Task →
algorithms + utils do the work → Excel/CSV +
an HTML map come out, with live progress.
Self-contained SVG · viewBox 3400×2620 (rendered 6800×5240) · layer-coloured across the package tree, class view & runtime. Based on the real com.storemapper source.
